explanation: The idea of a Constituent Assembly for India was first put forward by M.N. Roy in 1934. The Congress formally demanded it in 1935, the British accepted the principle in the August Offer (1940), and the Assembly was finally constituted under the Cabinet Mission Plan of 1946.
hint: Think of the radical thinker who first proposed it in 1934 — his initials are M.N.R.
source: NCERT Class 11 'Indian Constitution at Work', Ch.1 — Constitution: Why and How; M. Laxmikanth, Indian Polity — Making of the Constitution
stem: Who first proposed the idea of a Constituent Assembly for India?

explanation: The Constituent Assembly was constituted under the scheme formulated by the Cabinet Mission Plan of 1946. The Cripps Mission (1942) and August Offer (1940) only accepted the principle; the Wavell Plan dealt with the Viceroy's Executive Council.
hint: A three-member British mission visited India in 1946 and gave the scheme for the Assembly's composition.
source: NCERT Class 11 'Indian Constitution at Work', Ch.1; M. Laxmikanth, Indian Polity — Making of the Constitution
stem: Under which plan was the Constituent Assembly of India constituted?

explanation: The Constituent Assembly held its first meeting on 9 December 1946, with Dr. Sachchidanand Sinha as the interim president (the oldest member, following the French practice). Dr. Rajendra Prasad was elected permanent chairman two days later, on 11 December 1946.
hint: The Assembly first met in December 1946 — a few months before Independence.
source: NCERT Class 11 'Indian Constitution at Work', Ch.1; M. Laxmikanth, Indian Polity — Making of the Constitution
stem: When did the Constituent Assembly hold its first meeting?

explanation: Dr. Sachchidanand Sinha, the oldest member, was made the interim (temporary) president of the Assembly following the French practice. Later, on 11 December 1946, Dr. Rajendra Prasad was elected as its permanent chairman.
hint: The interim president was the oldest member of the Assembly — not the person who later became permanent chairman.
source: M. Laxmikanth, Indian Polity — Making of the Constitution; NCERT Class 11 'Indian Constitution at Work', Ch.1
stem: Who served as the interim president of the Constituent Assembly at its first meeting?

explanation: On 11 December 1946, Dr. Rajendra Prasad was elected the permanent chairman of the Constituent Assembly. H.C. Mukherjee and V.T. Krishnamachari served as its vice-presidents.
hint: He later became the first President of independent India.
source: M. Laxmikanth, Indian Polity — Making of the Constitution; NCERT Class 11 'Indian Constitution at Work', Ch.1
stem: Who was elected the permanent chairman of the Constituent Assembly?

explanation: The Objectives Resolution — the philosophy and guiding principles of the Constitution — was moved by Jawaharlal Nehru on 13 December 1946 and adopted by the Assembly on 22 January 1947. It later became the basis of the Preamble.
hint: It was moved by India's first Prime Minister in December 1946.
source: NCERT Class 11 'Indian Constitution at Work', Ch.1; M. Laxmikanth, Indian Polity — Philosophy of the Constitution
stem: Who moved the Objectives Resolution in the Constituent Assembly?

explanation: The Drafting Committee was set up on 29 August 1947 with Dr. B.R. Ambedkar as chairman. It had 7 members in total and was the most important committee — it prepared the draft Constitution.
hint: Its chairman is called the 'Father of the Indian Constitution'.
source: NCERT Class 11 'Indian Constitution at Work', Ch.1; M. Laxmikanth, Indian Polity — Making of the Constitution
stem: Who chaired the Drafting Committee of the Constituent Assembly?

explanation: The Drafting Committee consisted of 7 members including the chairman: B.R. Ambedkar, N. Gopalaswami Ayyangar, Alladi Krishnaswamy Ayyar, K.M. Munshi, Syed Mohammad Saadullah, N. Madhava Rau (replaced B.L. Mitter), and T.T. Krishnamachari (replaced D.P. Khaitan after his death).
hint: More than five, fewer than ten — the exact number is often asked directly.
source: M. Laxmikanth, Indian Polity — Making of the Constitution (Committees of the Constituent Assembly)
stem: How many members did the Drafting Committee have in total?

explanation: B.N. Rau was appointed as the Constitutional Adviser to the Constituent Assembly. He prepared the original draft of the Constitution for the Drafting Committee to work on. H.V.R. Iyengar was the Secretary of the Assembly.
hint: His initials are B.N.R. — he prepared the first draft the committee then debated.
source: M. Laxmikanth, Indian Polity — Making of the Constitution; NCERT Class 11 'Indian Constitution at Work', Ch.1
stem: Who was the Constitutional Adviser to the Constituent Assembly?

explanation: The Constitution was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on 26 November 1949 — which is why 26 November is celebrated as Constitution Day (Samvidhan Divas). Most provisions came into force later, on 26 January 1950.
hint: Adoption day is celebrated every year as Constitution Day — late November.
source: NCERT Class 11 'Indian Constitution at Work', Ch.1; M. Laxmikanth, Indian Polity — Making of the Constitution
stem: On which date was the Constitution of India adopted by the Constituent Assembly?

explanation: The Constitution came into force on 26 January 1950. This date was chosen to honour the Purna Swaraj (complete independence) declaration of 26 January 1930. Some provisions (citizenship, elections, provisional parliament) took effect on 26 November 1949 itself.
hint: The date honours the Purna Swaraj resolution of 1930 — late January.
source: NCERT Class 11 'Indian Constitution at Work', Ch.1; M. Laxmikanth, Indian Polity — Making of the Constitution
stem: When did the Constitution of India come into force?

explanation: At commencement, the Constitution contained 395 Articles grouped into 22 Parts with 8 Schedules. (Today it has grown to 25 Parts and 12 Schedules, with around 470 Articles.)
hint: The original figures are 395 — 22 — 8. Remember them as a set.
source: M. Laxmikanth, Indian Polity — Making of the Constitution; NCERT Class 11 'Indian Constitution at Work', Ch.1
stem: What was the original structure of the Constitution at commencement?

explanation: The Constituent Assembly took 2 years, 11 months and 18 days to complete its historic task — from the first meeting on 9 December 1946 to adoption on 26 November 1949.
hint: Just under three years — the exact phrase is '2 years, 11 months and 18 days'.
source: M. Laxmikanth, Indian Polity — Making of the Constitution
stem: How long did the Constituent Assembly take to frame the Constitution?

explanation: The Assembly originally had 389 members: 292 from the British provinces, 93 from the princely states, and 4 from the chief commissioner provinces. After Partition, the Muslim League members withdrew and the strength fell to 299.
hint: It started near 390 and fell to just under 300 after Partition.
source: M. Laxmikanth, Indian Polity — Making of the Constitution; NCERT Class 11 'Indian Constitution at Work', Ch.1
stem: What was the original strength of the Constituent Assembly, and what did it become after Partition?

explanation: Members of the Constituent Assembly were elected indirectly by the members of the provincial legislative assemblies (using proportional representation by single transferable vote). There was no universal adult franchise election for the Assembly.
hint: Ordinary citizens did not vote directly for Assembly members — the provincial assemblies chose them.
options: Directly elected by universal adult franchise
source: M. Laxmikanth, Indian Polity — Making of the Constitution; NCERT Class 11 'Indian Constitution at Work', Ch.1
stem: How were the members of the Constituent Assembly chosen?

explanation: The original Constitution was handwritten (calligraphed) by Prem Behari Narain Raizada in beautiful italic style, and each page was decorated by artists from Shantiniketan led by Nandalal Bose. It was not printed or typed.
hint: It was written by hand in flowing italic script — a famous calligrapher did the job.
options: It was typed on a typewriter
It was printed by the Government Press
It was drafted in English and translated by machine
It was handwritten by Prem Behari Narain Raizada
source: M. Laxmikanth, Indian Polity — Making of the Constitution
stem: Which of the following is true about the original manuscript of the Indian Constitution?

explanation: Under the Indian Independence Act 1947, the Constituent Assembly became a fully sovereign body and also functioned as the legislature (Dominion Legislature) — it made laws alongside framing the Constitution. When it met as the legislature, it was chaired by G.V. Mavalankar.
hint: Besides framing the Constitution, the Assembly also acted as the country's legislature after August 1947.
options: It also functioned as the Dominion Legislature
It was dissolved immediately after Independence
It reported to the British Parliament
source: M. Laxmikanth, Indian Polity — Making of the Constitution
stem: After the Indian Independence Act 1947, what additional role did the Constituent Assembly take on?

explanation: The Preamble is based on the Objectives Resolution moved by Nehru and adopted on 22 January 1947. The Resolution's ideals — sovereignty, democracy, justice, equality, freedom — were recast as the Preamble's opening statement.
hint: The Preamble's philosophy comes straight from a famous resolution Nehru moved in December 1946.
source: NCERT Class 11 'Indian Constitution at Work', Ch.1; M. Laxmikanth, Indian Polity — Philosophy of the Constitution
stem: The Preamble of the Indian Constitution is based on which of the following?

explanation: The Preamble opens with 'We, the people of India' — declaring that the ultimate sovereignty lies with the people, who adopt, enact and give themselves the Constitution. No external authority is the source of the Constitution.
hint: The opening words name who gives the Constitution to the nation.
source: NCERT Class 11 'Indian Constitution at Work', Ch.1; M. Laxmikanth, Indian Polity — Preamble of the Constitution
stem: According to the Preamble, from whom does the Constitution derive its authority?

explanation: The 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976 added three words to the Preamble: 'Socialist', 'Secular', and 'Integrity' (in 'unity and integrity of the Nation'). The original Preamble described India only as a 'Sovereign Democratic Republic'.
hint: Three words were inserted in 1976 during the Emergency — two describe the state's character, one joins 'unity'.
source: M. Laxmikanth, Indian Polity — Preamble of the Constitution; NCERT Class 11 'Indian Constitution at Work', Ch.2
stem: Which words were added to the Preamble by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976?

explanation: The Preamble declares India to be a 'Sovereign Socialist Secular Democratic Republic'. Each term is a basic feature: Sovereign (independent authority), Socialist (welfare-oriented mixed economy), Secular (equal treatment of all religions), Democratic (rule by the people), Republic (elected head of state).
hint: Five keywords — the last three letters of the sequence are S-S-D-R.
source: M. Laxmikanth, Indian Polity — Preamble of the Constitution; NCERT Class 11 'Indian Constitution at Work', Ch.2
stem: Which of the following correctly states how the Preamble describes India?

explanation: 'Sovereign' means India is free from the control of any foreign power — no external authority can dictate to it, and it can conduct its own internal and foreign affairs independently.
hint: It is about freedom from any outside power's control.
options: India has an official state religion
India's head of state is hereditary
India is free from external control
source: M. Laxmikanth, Indian Polity — Preamble of the Constitution
stem: What does 'Sovereign' in the Preamble signify?

explanation: 'Secular' means the Indian state treats all religions equally — it has no official religion, neither favours nor discriminates against any religion. (Added to the Preamble by the 42nd Amendment, though the principle was always part of the Constitution.)
hint: It is about the state's relationship with religion — equal treatment for all.
options: The state promotes one official religion
The state treats all religions equally
The state bans all religious practices
The state is run by religious leaders
source: M. Laxmikanth, Indian Polity — Preamble of the Constitution; NCERT Class 11 'Indian Constitution at Work', Ch.2
stem: What does 'Secular' in the Preamble mean?

explanation: In a 'Republic', the head of state is elected (directly or indirectly) for a fixed term, rather than inheriting the position like a monarch. India's President is elected by an electoral college.
hint: Contrast with a monarchy — how does the head of state get the job?
options: The Prime Minister is the head of state
The judiciary elects the head of state
The head of state inherits the position
The head of state is elected
source: M. Laxmikanth, Indian Polity — Preamble of the Constitution
stem: What does 'Republic' in the Preamble signify?

explanation: The Preamble promises Justice — social, economic and political. Social justice means equal treatment without discrimination; economic justice means fair distribution of wealth; political justice means equal political rights.
hint: Three kinds — think society, economy, and politics.
source: M. Laxmikanth, Indian Polity — Preamble of the Constitution; NCERT Class 11 'Indian Constitution at Work', Ch.2
stem: The Preamble secures 'Justice' of which three kinds to all citizens?

explanation: The Preamble guarantees Liberty of thought, expression, belief, faith and worship. These freedoms are not absolute — reasonable restrictions apply (developed in the Fundamental Rights chapter).
hint: Five items — what you think, say, believe in, have faith in, and how you worship.
options: Thought, expression, belief, faith and worship
source: M. Laxmikanth, Indian Polity — Preamble of the Constitution
stem: Liberty in the Preamble covers which of the following?

explanation: The Preamble promises 'Equality of status and of opportunity' — equal standing before the law and an equal chance to develop, regardless of birth. It does not promise identical income or identical outcomes.
hint: Two things: your standing, and your chance — not identical wealth.
options: Equality of income for all citizens
Equality of status and of opportunity
source: M. Laxmikanth, Indian Polity — Preamble of the Constitution
stem: What kind of 'Equality' does the Preamble promise?

explanation: Fraternity in the Preamble means a sense of brotherhood among all Indians, 'assuring the dignity of the individual and the unity and integrity of the Nation'. The word 'integrity' was added by the 42nd Amendment in 1976.
hint: It is about brotherhood — and it assures two things: dignity of the individual and unity of the nation.
options: Loyalty to one's own state only
Brotherhood assuring individual dignity and national unity
source: M. Laxmikanth, Indian Polity — Preamble of the Constitution
stem: What does 'Fraternity' in the Preamble assure?

explanation: In the Berubari Union case (1960), the Supreme Court held the Preamble is NOT a part of the Constitution. In Kesavananda Bharati (1973), it reversed itself and held the Preamble IS a part of the Constitution — the Berubari view was overruled.
hint: The 1960 view said 'not a part'; the landmark 1973 case reversed it.
options: Berubari said no, Kesavananda said yes
Both cases said it is not a part
Both cases said it is a part
Kesavananda said no, Berubari said yes
source: M. Laxmikanth, Indian Polity — Preamble of the Constitution
stem: Which statement correctly describes the Supreme Court's position on whether the Preamble is part of the Constitution?

explanation: The Preamble is non-justiciable — its provisions are not enforceable in a court of law. Neither the legislature nor courts can be compelled to follow it directly, though courts use it to interpret ambiguous provisions (LIC of India case, 1995: it is an integral part but not a source of power).
hint: Can a citizen go to court saying 'my Preamble rights were violated'? No — that is the key word for this question.
options: It is enforceable like a Fundamental Right
It is non-justiciable (not enforceable in court)
It applies only to the Union government
source: M. Laxmikanth, Indian Polity — Preamble of the Constitution
stem: What is the legal enforceability of the Preamble?
